title: Violin lessons and turning professional at 17
summary: De Fuentes taught him violin, then a Frenchman named Ferdinand; he turned professional around 17 and played only violin until about 1918.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: That is, yes. He first taught me violin, you know. And then I had an, after he got through, I had a Frenchman from over in the city. He used to come over and give me lessons. When I was a kid, then I was around about in my teens then, you know, 14, 15, like that. When I got about, well, 17, I started to play professionally, you know. Playing in bands, dances, doing stuff. Nothing.
What was this teacher's name from across the river, the Frenchman?
Well, I know it was Ferdinand, but I can't think of his last name, you know. He was from France. I have a manuscript there that he wrote. I think his name is on it. I'll show it to you before you go.
Oh, I would like very much to see it. Now, you've got a fine collection of things. You showed me some of your pictures.

Mm-hmm. Quite a bit of pictures, yeah. Well, I played the violin, man, until about, about 1918 I started playing brass, you know. Mm-hmm. But all the former years I played nothing but the violin, you know.
Yeah, when I was with Bunk and them.
Had you ever played anything else, guitar, bass?
